emergency conditions.

developed under this order. Modifications and temporary organiza­
tion changes, based on emergency conditions, w ill be in accordance 
with policy determination by the President.

to the President.

latter shall control. Emergency Preparedness Orders Nos. 4 and 5

ization) (26 F.R. 656-658), are hereby revoked.

objectives, the Secretary shall supervise or conduct research in areas 
directly concerned with carrying out emergency preparedness re­
sponsibilities for health, education, and welfare programs. W ith 
respect to the emergency health and welfare services assigmnent, this 
is defined as, but not limited to (1) development of medical means 
for the prevention and care of casualties (including those from 
thermonuclear weapons, radiation exposure, and biological and 
chemical warfare, as well as from other weapons); (2) research in 
preventive medicines, basic biology and environmental sanitation 
directed to maintaining the health of noncasualty population; (3) 
pre-attack and post-attack target research in health services; (4) 
protection o f resources and protocol essential to carrying out long­
term basic and applied research in the post-attack period; and (5) 
the development o f techniques for the most efficient utilization of 
civilian health manpower. Designate representatives for necessary 
ad hoc or task force groups and provide advice and assistance to other 
agencies in planning for research in areas involving the Department’s 
interest.
Sec. 13. Functional Guidance.  The Secretary, in carrying out the  
functions assigned in this order, shall be guided by the following:
(a ) Interagency cooperation.  The Secretary shall assume the initi­
ative in developing joint plans for the coordination of emergency 
civilian health services and welfare services programs of those depart­
ments and agencies which have responsibility for any segment of such 
activities. H e shall utilize to the maximum those capabilities of other 
agencies qualified to perform or assist in the performance of assigned 
functions by contractual or other agreements.
(b) Presidential coordination.  The Director o f the Office o f Emer­
gency Planning shall advise and assist the President in determining 
policy for, and assist him in coordinating the performance of functions 
under this order with the total national preparedness program.
(c) Em ergency planning.  Emergency plans and programs, and 
emergency organization structure required thereby, shall be developed 
as an integral part of the continuing activities o f the Department of 
Health, Education, and W elfare on the basis that it w ill have the 
responsibility for carrying out such programs during an emergency. 
The Secretary shall be prepared to implement all appropriate plans 
developed under this order. Modifications and temporary organiza­
tion changes, based on emergency conditions, w ill be in accordance 
with policy determination by the President.

strued as conferring authority under Title I I I  o f the Federal Civil

emergency plan, procedure, policy, program, or course o f action pre­
pared or developed pursuant to this order. Such authority is reserved 
to the President.

delegate within the Department of Health, Education, and W elfare 
the functions hereinabove assigned to him.

versions.research_rationale: EO 11001 (signed 1962-02-16, 27 FR 1534-1538), read in full from the held official FR text: Sec. 1 Scope: health services, civilian health manpower, health resources, welfare services, educational programs; Sec. 2 Definitions (a)-(e); Sec. 3 Health Functions (a)-(h); Sec. 4 Welfare Functions (a)-(e); Sec. 5 Education Functions; Sec. 6 Facilities Protection and Damage Assessment (a)-(b); Sec. 7 Resources; Sec. 8 Relative Urgencies; Sec. 9 Requirements; Sec. 10 Claimancy; Sec. 11 Stockpiles; Sec. 12 Research; Sec. 13 Functional Guidance (a)-(c); Sec. 14 Emergency Actions (no authority to put plans into effect); Sec. 15 Redelegation; Sec. 16 Prior Actions (this order controls over inconsistent prior orders; Emergency Preparedness Orders Nos. 4 and 5 revoked). It has no term or sunset. EO 11490 sec. 3015 item (9) revokes it, effective on signing 1969-10-28 (official text, PDF page 95). Inventory: the dossier's clauses omit the Sec. 1 Scope and some section lead-ins and run some sections together; one override restates the inventory as 16 section clauses with no gap or overlap from Sec. 1 to the end of the Prior Actions section. D6 / earlier-end and later-amendment test: the OFR catalog records a 'See' note to EO 10952 (the 1961 civil-defense order the text cites) and the EO 11490 revocation; the OLRC note at 42 U.S.C. 5195 records only the EO 11490 revocation; the by-number scan of all 6,652 held FR order texts finds no order naming EO 11001: the hits are its own heading printed at the end of EO 11000's held page text, citations of 42 U.S.C. 11001 (EPCRA) in EO 12856, 12898, 12969, 13148, 13514, 13693 and 14096, the FR page 90 FR 11001 (EO 14220) and index page numbers in EO 9602; the full EO 11490 text names it only in sec. 3015. EO 11051 (1962-09-27) sec. 601 does not list it, and none of EO 11087-11095 (February 26, 1963) or EO 11310 (1966) names it. No order amended, suspended or ended any clause between 1962-02-16 and 1969-10-28, so no later event is attached. The Prior Actions section's revocation of an OCDM Emergency Preparedness Order was executed on issuance; revoking this order does not revive it. savings_residuals.reason: Reading record LSP-EO_11490 (EO 11490, 34 FR 17567-17599, official FR text of FR-1969-10-30.pdf PDF pages 63-95 held by jobs/source-ladder, read in full; the American Presidency Project transcription was not used): sec. 101 says the order 'consolidates the assignment of emergency preparedness functions to various departments and agencies heretofore contained in the 21 Executive orders and 2 Defense Mobilization orders listed in Section 3015' and that 'Assignments have been adjusted to conform to changes in organization'; sec. 102(b) charges every department and agency with continuity-of-government planning; Parts 2-29 re-assign agency functions (Part 6 Post Office, Part 7 Interior, Part 8 Agriculture, Part 10 Labor, Part 11 Health, Education, and Welfare, Part 13 Transportation including civil aviation, Part 18 FCC including electromagnetic-radiation control of non-Government stations); Part 30 sets general provisions. Sec. 3014 ('Retention of Existing Authority') preserves existing assignments of functions 'Except as provided in Section 3015', so it expressly does not reach the revoked orders; sec. 3015 revokes 21 Executive orders and 2 Defense Mobilization orders without exception. There is no effective-date, pending-matter, transition or savings clause for any revoked order. Own-residual check, reading EO 11001 in full: it assigned to the Secretary of Health, Education, and Welfare national emergency preparedness planning functions (scope, functions, cooperation with the Department of Defense under EO 10952, research, functional guidance), disclaimed any authority to put plans into effect (Emergency Actions), allowed redelegation, and in its Prior Actions section revoked OCDM Emergency Preparedness Order Nos. 4 and 5 (26 F.R. 656-658). EO 11490 Part 11 (Department of Health, Education, and Welfare) re-assigns the same department's or agency's emergency preparedness functions, adjusted to later changes in organization (sec. 101); that is a new assignment by the consolidating order, not a continuation of EO 11001. Plans and programs developed before 1969-10-28 are completed acts. The revocation of Emergency Preparedness Order Nos. 4 and 5 (26 F.R. 656-658) was executed in 1962 and is not undone by revoking EO 11001. State transferred_or_accrued records the carry-forward of the assignment into EO 11490; no clause of EO 11001 continues.
